chats.activity.mdDescription:
Say what the caller is doing in a chat, live; yields activity { activity } — never a message (CHAT-18).

By a participant: `started` (it has the message), `working` (the
default: a line of what it does now, or a heartbeat with none),
`ended` (the turn is over). Every participant's `watch` hears
`activity`; nothing is stored — the server keeps each chat's last
200 in memory for `activity_log`, lost on a restart. A line is cut
at 500 characters. A chat the caller is not in is `not_found`.

mdParams.pdDescription: The chat, e.g. 41.
What it does now, e.g. `Read src/queue.rs` (optional).
started | working | ended (optional; default working).

chats.activity_log.mdDescription:
A chat's live work kept in memory — its last 200 activity items, oldest first; an activity { activity } each, then the end (CHAT-18).

For a participant, so a viewer opening a chat mid-turn sees what has
been done; anyone else is answered `not_found`. Empty after a restart.

mdParams.pdDescription: The chat, e.g. 41.

chats.add.mdDescription:
Add a participant to a chat; yields added { chat }.

By a participant, to an open chat; the one added must be able to read
the ticket, or it is `refused`. One already in it is the chat as it is.
CHAT-14: to a group, one holding a grant in its organization, by a
participant or an admin of the organization; a direct message is
refused (it stays between two: start a group). CHAT-16: an admin of
the chat's scope adds anyone, in it or not; one who can't read it is
added only with `grant` — `ticket` (viewer on the ticket alone) or
`chat` (this chat only) — the add and the grant one write, answered
`added { chat, granted }`; without it, `needs_grant { choices }` and
nothing written.

mdParams.pdDescription: The chat, e.g. 41.
What an admin grants one who can't read the chat's ticket: ticket | chat (optional; CHAT-16).
Who to add: a principal.

chats.await_message.mdDescription:
Wait for the next message for the caller: waiting at once, then one message { message } by someone else — in the chat named, or any of the caller's chats (on ticket, when named) — or one answered { … } to an input in the caller's own messages (input: that one alone), and the end; timed_out after timeout_minutes.

The first message after `since` (unix seconds, at or after it; without
it, after the call) and after the message `after` by anyone but the
caller — so a reconnect with the `since` that `waiting` said, or the
last message it read as `after` (exact, where a second can hold two
messages), loses nothing. While it waits, the chats it waits on
show the caller as `listening` on `watch`. A chat the caller is not
in is `not_found`.

mdParams.pdDescription: Only messages after this one — the last the caller read (optional).
The chat, e.g. 41 (optional; default any of the caller's).
Only the answer to this input, `<message>/<input>`, e.g. 812/undated (optional; CHAT-20).
Messages from this unix time, so a reconnect loses nothing (optional; default now).
Only the caller's chats on this ticket (optional).
Give up after this many minutes with timed_out (optional; default never).

chats.candidates.mdDescription:
Who could be in a chat — on a ticket, or (without one) outside tickets: a candidate { principal, reads, name?, agent } each — every principal holding a grant in the organization (a team's members by name), and those in the caller's chats there — then the end.

CHAT-4's picker: `reads` says whether the principal can read the
ticket now (`open` and `add` refuse one that cannot). The caller is
not among them. A ticket the caller cannot read is `refused` as one
that is none. A participant who holds no grant there now (one kept
before ACCESS-24, when login could be off) is listed all the same, as
one of the chats' participants. CHAT-14: without a ticket, those
holding a grant in the caller's organizations (`reads`: may be in a
direct message or a group); each by the `name` the server knows it
by (signed in with — a synapse key's name too), and `agent` for an
agent (an `agent:` or `key:` principal, or a standing chat member).

mdParams.pdDescription: The ticket, e.g. KILN-7 (optional: none for who may be in a direct message or a group).

chats.close.mdDescription:
Close a chat; yields closed { chat }. A closed chat is read-only, kept on its ticket.

By any participant. Closing a closed chat changes nothing.

mdParams.pdDescription: The chat, e.g. 41.

chats.delete.mdDescription:
Delete messages in a chat — kept and marked deleted { at, by }, never gone; yields messages_deleted { chat, ids, by, at, unread } (CHAT-44).

A message's author deletes it, and an admin of the chat's ticket
(outside tickets, of its organization) deletes any. Name them by
`ids`, or every message of the chat from `from` to `to`. All or
none: one the caller may not delete, or not the chat's, is
`refused`, naming each; one already deleted is not named again.
`messages` still answers a deleted message, marked; it is no one's
unread and no `await_message` reply. `watch` carries
`messages_deleted` to every participant.

mdParams.pdDescription: The chat, e.g. 6.
The first of a range of the chat's messages (optional; with to).
The messages, e.g. 245,247 (optional: or from and to).
The last of the range, included (optional; with from).

chats.inputs.answer.mdDescription:
Answer a message's input — a value checked against its kind and options, with a rationale; who, the source and the time said by the server; yields input_changed { input }.

By a participant of the chat, while the chat is open and the message
kept. The value is typed as `tickets inputs answer`'s:
`{"type": "choice", "option": …}`, `{"type": "multi", "options": […]}`,
`{"type": "text", "text": …}`. Every answer is a history entry. A
closed input, a value that does not answer it, or one the caller may
not give is `refused { reasons }`, and nothing is written. `watch`
carries the `input_changed` to every participant; it answers an
`await_message` waiting on it.

mdParams.pdDescription: The chat, e.g. 12.
The input's id in that message's body, e.g. undated.
The message that asks, e.g. 812.
Why (optional).

Typed by the input's kind: {"type": "choice", "option": "keep"} | {"type": "multi", "options": ["a", "b"]} | {"type": "text", "text": "a reply"}; through synapse, --value.type choice --value.option keep.

chats.inputs.clear.mdDescription:
Clear a message's input's answer (open again; kept in its history); yields input_changed { input }, or input { input } when it held none.

By the one who gave the answer (any participant, for an answer kept
before who answered was), while the chat is open. A closed input is
`refused`.

mdParams.pdDescription: The chat, e.g. 12.
The input's id in that message's body.
The message that asks, e.g. 812.

chats.inputs.close.mdDescription:
Close a message's input: freeze its answer (DECIDED, for a decision); yields input_changed { input }, or input { input } when it was closed.

By the message's author — who asked — or an admin of the chat's
ticket. An answer or a clear is refused until it is reopened.

mdParams.pdDescription: The chat, e.g. 12.
The input's id in that message's body.
The message that asks, e.g. 812.

chats.inputs.list.mdDescription:
The inputs of the messages in the caller's chats (an <m-decision id> / <m-input id kind> in a message's body), oldest message first; an input { input } each, then page { next }.

Each with its home (chat, message, the chat's ticket, who asked),
kind, question, options, recommendation, state, answer (`by`, `name`,
`source`, `at_unix`) and whole history. `chat` one chat (one the
caller does not see is `not_found`), else every chat the caller is
in; `ticket` only chats on it. `after` (a message id) continues a
page; `limit` 100 unless given, at most 1,000 — a message's inputs
are never split. A deleted message's are not listed.

mdParams.pdDescription: Cursor: the inputs of messages after this one (optional).
Only this chat's, e.g. 12 (optional).
Only inputs of this kind: choice | multi | text (optional).
At most this many inputs (default 100, at most 1000) (optional).
Only inputs in this state: open | answered | closed (optional).
Only chats on this ticket, e.g. KILN-40 (optional).

chats.inputs.reopen.mdDescription:
Reopen a closed message's input; yields input_changed { input }, or input { input } when it was not closed.

By the message's author or an admin of the chat's ticket: `answered`
again when it holds an answer, else `open`.

mdParams.pdDescription: The chat, e.g. 12.
The input's id in that message's body.
The message that asks, e.g. 812.

chats.inputs.schema.mdDescription: Get plugin or method schema. Pass {"method": "name"} for a specific method.

chats.link.mdDescription:
Link tickets to a chat, as a builder's work from it; yields linked { chat, tickets, how } — those new to it (CHAT-55).

By a participant; each ticket one the caller reads, or the call is
`refused`, naming each, and nothing is linked. `watch` carries
`linked` to every participant.

mdParams.pdDescription: The chat, e.g. 6.
The tickets, e.g. CHAT-55,CHAT-56.

chats.list.mdDescription:
The caller's chats, by last activity, newest first — on a ticket, with or without unread, open or closed; a chat { chat } each, then page { next }.

Without `ticket`, the chats the caller is in; with it, those on that
ticket the caller is in — every one there, for an admin of it. Each
chat's `unread` is the caller's. `after` (a chat id) continues a page;
`limit` is 50 unless given, at most 500.

mdParams.pdDescription: Cursor: continue after this chat (optional).
At most this many chats (default 50, at most 500) (optional).
Only chats in this state: open | closed (optional).
Only chats on this ticket, e.g. KILN-7 (optional).
Only chats with unread messages for the caller (true), or without (false) (optional).

chats.messages.mdDescription:
A page of a chat's messages, oldest first within it; a message { message } each, then page { next }.

For a participant (or an admin of its ticket); anyone else is
answered `not_found`. `after` (a message id) pages forward, `next`
the page's last while newer remain. CHAT-8: `newest: true` is the
newest page, and `before` (a message id) pages back from one — `next`
the page's first while older remain, what `before` takes to go on.
`limit` is 100 unless given, at most 1,000.

mdParams.pdDescription: Cursor: the messages after this one (optional).
Cursor: the messages before this one, the nearest last (optional; CHAT-8).
The chat, e.g. 41.
At most this many messages (default 100, at most 1000) (optional).
The newest page (optional; CHAT-8).

chats.open.mdDescription:
Open a chat on a ticket, or outside tickets — a direct message or a group — with the principals named; yields opened { chat } — the open chat they already have, when they do (existing: true).

The caller and `others` are the participants (CHAT-1's `with`, which
TypeScript does not take as a parameter's name). On a ticket,
`others` empty or absent is a chat of one, the caller's alone, to
add to later (CHAT-6); every one of them must be able to read the
ticket, or the call is `refused { reasons }`, naming each who cannot,
and nothing is made. A ticket the caller cannot read is refused as
one that is none. DEPLOY-47: on a ticket, a `title` finds only their
open chat of that title — a chat per subject. CHAT-14: without a ticket, one other is a direct
message (the one the two have, when they have one) and several a
group (`title` names it); each must hold a grant in the caller's
organization, and only its participants read it. `watch` carries
`opened` to each participant.

mdParams.pdDescription: Who else is in it: principals, each able to read the ticket (on a ticket, none or absent: a chat of one; without one: one for a direct message, several for a group).
The ticket the chat is about, e.g. KILN-7 (optional: none for a direct message or a group).
A title for it (optional).

chats.post.mdDescription:
Post a message in a chat; yields posted { message, inputs }, signed by the caller.

Only a participant posts; a closed chat is `refused`. The body is markdown, not blank, at most the ticket body cap; its `<m-decision id>` / `<m-input id kind>`
are inputs, born `open` (CHAT-20; a malformed one refuses the post). A chat the caller
does not see is `not_found`. `watch` carries `posted` to every participant, and it answers their `await_message`. CHAT-66: a body
that starts `[↩](message:N)` replies to N — its `reply_to` and `quote`; N outside this chat is `refused`, naming it.

mdParams.pdDescription: What it says (markdown).
The chat, e.g. 41.

chats.read.mdDescription:
Mark a chat read up to a message; yields read { chat, upto, unread }.

Moves the caller's own mark forward (never back) to the latest of
the chat's messages at or before `upto`; `unread` counts after it.
`watch` carries `read` to the caller's other watches.

mdParams.pdDescription: The chat, e.g. 52.
The last message read, e.g. 7.

chats.remove.mdDescription:
Take a participant out of a chat; yields removed { chat, principal, revoked } (CHAT-14; CHAT-16: revoke takes back the grant their add made).

A group's or a ticket's chat, by a participant (itself too: it
leaves) or, outside tickets, an admin of the chat's organization; a
direct message is refused (close it instead). One not in it is the
chat as it is. The one removed hears `left` on its `watch`.

mdParams.pdDescription: The chat, e.g. 41.
Who to take out: a principal.
Also revoke the grant their add made (an admin's; optional; CHAT-16).

chats.rename.mdDescription:
Rename a chat; yields renamed { chat } — the composer's /title (CHAT-7).

By any participant. No title, or a blank one, clears it (the chat is
then named by who is in it). The same title changes nothing.

mdParams.pdDescription: The chat, e.g. 41.
Its title (optional: none clears it).

chats.reopen.mdDescription:
Reopen a closed chat; yields reopened { chat }.

By any participant. Reopening an open chat changes nothing.

mdParams.pdDescription: The chat, e.g. 41.

chats.restore.mdDescription:
Put deleted messages back in a chat; yields messages_restored { chat, ids, by, at, unread } (CHAT-44).

`delete`'s rule: a message's author, or an admin of the chat's
ticket (outside tickets, its organization); by `ids`, or `from` …
`to`; all or none. One not deleted is not named again. `watch`
carries `messages_restored` to every participant.

mdParams.pdDescription: The chat, e.g. 6.
The first of a range of the chat's messages (optional; with to).
The messages, e.g. 245,247 (optional: or from and to).
The last of the range, included (optional; with from).

chats.schema.mdDescription: Get plugin or method schema. Pass {"method": "name"} for a specific method.

chats.tickets.mdDescription:
The tickets a chat names — in its messages, filed from it or linked to it — each a ticket { ticket } with its stage, newest first (CHAT-55).

A message's codes count from when it is posted (a deleted message's
drop out); `tickets create --chat` and `link` add theirs. Only the
tickets the caller reads; a chat it does not see is `not_found`.
The stage: waits_on_you, ready, in_progress, in_review, on_test,
shipped (closed, other: not work in hand).

mdParams.pdDescription: The chat, e.g. 6.

chats.watch.mdDescription:
Subscribe to the caller's chats: opened, posted, added, read, closed, reopened, messages_deleted, messages_restored, listening, left — until disconnect.

The chats the caller is in (with `ticket`, those on it — every one
there for an admin of it), each change as the caller sees it: its own
unread, its own `read`s. A chat whose ticket leaves the caller's
reach is said once as `left { chat }`. ACCESS-12: the caller is
verified again as its grants move; refused, the watch ends with
`watch_closed { reason, message }`. `lagged { missed }` where a slow
subscriber lost changes.

mdParams.pdDescription: Only chats on this ticket, e.g. KILN-7 (optional).

comments.add.mdDescription:
Leave a comment at an anchor (route, path, label, excerpt, and ticket when the element belongs to one); yields the comment.

Keeps a comment: `anchor` says where it was left — `route` (the app
page, beginning `#/`), `path` (where on the page), `label` and
`excerpt` (what was there, in words; the excerpt may be empty), and
`ticket` when the element belongs to one, which must name a ticket
and is kept with that ticket's `updated_unix` as `version` (set by
the server). ACCESS-19: the comment is signed by the caller — its
principal kept, its name the author (the principal when it has no
name; `owner` on one kept before ACCESS-24, when login could be off);
no call names its author. Yields
exactly one event: `comment` — the comment as kept: its id, state
`open`, the time (`at`, unix seconds), the author, its anchor and
body — or an in-band `error` naming the problem (an empty body, a
malformed anchor, a ticket that is none), with nothing kept. `watch`
carries `added`. IDENTITY-37: a comment left on a ticket's page
(`route` `#/ticket/X`) is `X`'s to see whatever its anchor names — the
caller needs the role on `X` as well as on the anchor's ticket, and it
is listed and watched only by those who can view both. The anchor is
kept as given (`ticket` stays what the element belonged to).
ACCESS-19: a comment on the app (naming no ticket) is seen only by
its author and the admins of `*`. COMMENT-8: with `reply_to`, a reply
to that comment — no anchor (one given is refused): it takes its
thread's root's, and so its ticket and who sees it; a reply to a
reply answers the same root; a resolved root is reopened in the same
write (`watch` carries `added`, then `reopened`). The answer carries
`reply_to`, the root's id.

mdParams.pdDescription: Where: {route: '#/ticket/DEMAND-2', path: '[data-tag="ticket DEMAND-1"]', label: 'Parent chip', excerpt: 'DEMAND-1', ticket: 'DEMAND-2' (optional)}; version is set by the server. Required unless reply_to is given.
What it says (markdown; not empty, at most 64 KiB).
COMMENT-8: the comment this answers, e.g. 29 — the reply takes its thread's anchor (optional).

comments.failures.mdDescription:
COMMENT-9: the comments the app could not keep, newest first — `failure { failure }` each.

The caller's own reports and those whose comment it would see had it
been kept; at most `limit` (default 50, at most 200).

mdParams.pdDescription: At most this many (default 50, at most 200) (optional).

comments.list.mdDescription:
List comments, newest first, filtered by ticket, under (a ticket or shortcode's lineage), route, path (a prefix), state, author and text; paged with after + limit.

The comments matching every filter given, newest first — one
`comment` event each — then exactly one `page { next }`: `next` is
the id to pass as the next call's `after`, `null` when nothing more
matches. `after` starts the page strictly after (older than) that
comment; `limit` caps it (ACCESS-29: 500 unless given, at most 1,000,
[`crate::limits`]). The filters:
`ticket` (the anchor's ticket), `under` (a ticket or a shortcode: the
comment's ticket is in its lineage — itself, its ancestors, its
shortcode and the shortcodes hosting it — as the filter language's
`under`, read as the tree stands now), `route` (exactly), `path` (a
prefix of the anchor's), `state` (`open` or `resolved`), `author`
(exactly) and `text` (in the body, the label or the excerpt, whatever
its ASCII case) and `intent` (APP-23: `comment` or `changes`). A blank filter is none. An unknown `state`, or an
`after` that names no comment, is one in-band `error` and nothing
else. Only the comments the caller sees (ACCESS-10; a comment on the
app, its author's and the admins' of `*`). From the cache.

mdParams.pdDescription: Cursor: start strictly after (older than) this comment id (optional).
Only comments by this author, exactly (optional).
Only comments of this intent: comment | changes (APP-23: a change request) (optional).
At most this many comments (default 500, at most 1000); the page event carries the next cursor (optional).
Only comments whose anchor's path begins with this (optional; through synapse pass it with -p — synapse expands a `path` flag as a file path).
Only comments on this app page, exactly, e.g. #/ticket/DEMAND-2 (optional).
Only comments in this state: open | resolved (optional).
Only comments with this text in the body, the label or the excerpt, any ASCII case (optional).
COMMENT-8: only this comment's thread — its root and the root's replies, oldest last as every page (optional).
Only comments on this ticket, e.g. DEMAND-2 (optional).
Only comments whose ticket is in this one's lineage: a ticket (it and its descendants) or a shortcode (it and every shortcode hosted under it), e.g. FILTER (optional).

comments.reopen.mdDescription:
Reopen a resolved comment; yields the comment, open.

Yields exactly one event: `comment`, state `open` — as it was, if it
already was — or an in-band `error` for an id that names no comment.
A comment the caller does not see is answered as one that is not
there, naming nothing (ACCESS-3 #7). `watch` carries `reopened`.

mdParams.pdDescription: The comment's id, e.g. 1.

comments.report.mdDescription:
COMMENT-9: report a comment the app could not keep; yields `reported { failure }`.

The app's word that a comment was not kept — the socket down, no
answer, a refusal — with the draft, so whoever can see where it was
being left reads it with `failures`. Kept in memory (the newest 200;
a restart forgets them) and logged; never a comment.

mdParams.pdDescription: The browser, as it names itself (optional).
Where the comment was being left, as `add`'s anchor.
What it said (cut to 64 KiB).
When it failed, unix seconds (optional: now).
Why it was not kept, in the app's words.

comments.resolve.mdDescription:
Resolve a comment; yields the comment, resolved.

Yields exactly one event: `comment`, state `resolved` — as it was,
if it already was, and then nothing is written or broadcast — or an
in-band `error` for an id that names no comment. A comment the
caller does not see is answered as one that is not there, naming
nothing (ACCESS-3 #7). `watch` carries `resolved`.

mdParams.pdDescription: The comment's id, e.g. 1.

comments.schema.mdDescription: Get plugin or method schema. Pass {"method": "name"} for a specific method.

comments.watch.mdDescription:
Subscribe to comments: added / resolved / reopened, each with the comment, until disconnect; lagged { missed } where a slow subscriber lost changes.

`added`, `resolved` and `reopened`, each with the comment as the
change left it, in the order the writes were acknowledged, until the
client goes; `lagged { missed }` where a slow subscriber lost changes
(`list` again to catch up). Nothing a ticket's write does is here —
that is `tickets.watch`. IDENTITY-37: what it relays follows the
caller's grants as they stand at each change, and a caller who can
see nothing any more is told so in band and the stream ends —
ACCESS-12: with one `watch_closed { reason, message }`, at once when
a revoke or sign-out ends it.

deployments.environments.mdDescription: Each environment: what it runs, since when, its last deployment, how many tickets run there
deployments.environments.mdLongDescription:
Every environment — of `project` when given — one `environment`
event each, by project and then in display order (test → staging →
prod): what it runs, since when, its last deployment, how many
tickets run there, and (DEPLOY-21) `from`, where it promotes from.

mdParams.pdDescription: Only this project's (a shortcode) (optional)

deployments.for_ticket.mdDescription: Where a ticket's work runs: running { environment, since, deployment, behind, version } per environment, not_running for the rest
deployments.for_ticket.mdLongDescription:
Where a ticket's work runs: one `running` event for each environment
it runs in — since when, brought by which deployment, what the
environment runs now — and one `not_running` for each other
environment of its projects (its shortcode's, its hosts', and any it
has run in). DEPLOY-20: a `running` whose `behind` is not empty runs
an earlier version there — `behind` the commits not carried, in link
order, `version` the newest carried one. An `error` for an id that
names no ticket.

mdParams.pdDescription: Ticket id, e.g. MENGER-34

deployments.list.mdDescription: List deployments newest first, by project, environment, state and ticket; each with the tickets it carried
deployments.list.mdLongDescription:
The deployments matching every filter given, newest first — one
`deployment` event each (with the tickets it carried, its unlinked
commits, and `live`: whether it still counts in its environment) —
then exactly one `page { next }`. `after` starts strictly after
(older than) that deployment; `limit` caps the page. From the cache.

mdParams.pdDescription: Cursor: start strictly after (older than) this deployment id (optional)
Only to this environment (optional)
At most this many; the page event carries the next cursor (optional)
Only this project's (a shortcode) (optional)
Only in this state: started | succeeded | failed | rolled_back | requested (optional)
Only those that carried this ticket (optional)

deployments.running.mdDescription: The kept cells: cells { project, environment, running: [{ ticket, since, deployment, behind, version }], staged: [{ ticket, stage }] } per environment
deployments.running.mdLongDescription:
DEPLOY-13: the kept cells — one `cells { project, environment,
running }` per environment (of `project`, named `environment`, when
given), `running` every ticket there (only `ids`' when given, at most
1,000), each with since when and the deploy that brought it, in the
store's order — an empty one too, so a copy can replace what it held.

Keep an image for a ticket (PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, at most 7 MiB, base64); yields stored { hash, mime, bytes, width, height, duplicate }.

(an image travels as base64 in one WebSocket message, whose limit is

the same bytes were kept already (one row: nothing new is stored but,
for a second ticket, that it is that one's too) — or `refused {
reason, message, bytes?, max? }` (`too_large`, `not_an_image`,
`type_mismatch`, `truncated`, `bad_data`), naming why, with nothing

(README "Comments").

tickets.create.mdDescription:
Create a ticket; allocates the next EPIC-N id, status starts Pending (a doc's: Doc, for good); the first ticket of a prefix must be a scope or a doc.

Creates a ticket in an epic. The store allocates the next `EPIC-N`
id; status starts at `Pending` (only a human promotes to `Ready`);
`kind` defaults to `build`, and one outside the six yields the
in-band error naming them. SDLC-11: a `doc` starts — and stays — in
`Doc`; it may be a shortcode's first ticket, as a scope may; a doc
with a `blocked_by`, a `blocked_by` naming a doc, and a doc born as
an id some `blocked_by` already names are in-band errors (a doc never
completes, so nothing may wait on one). `parent` (AGS-19) files the ticket as an
output of an existing ticket in any epic; one that names no ticket,
or that would make the newborn its own ancestor, is an in-band error
naming the reason. MNG-14: omitted, `parent` defaults to the
shortcode's scope root; given, it must be inside the same shortcode
— except for the scope root itself, whose parent is the shortcode
it hangs under. Every shortcode starts with a scope (MNG-12) or a
doc (SDLC-11): the first ticket of a prefix must be `kind: scope` or
`kind: doc`, and anything else is an in-band error naming the rule,
with nothing allocated. WAVE-10: `path` gives the ticket a path
address in its shortcode (`<SHORTCODE>/<path>`, which `get` resolves)
— accepted only when it starts with `_MENGER/` and names something
after it, `kind` is `doc`, and `parent` is the shortcode's scope root
(or omitted, which defaults to it); a path another ticket of the
shortcode already holds is an in-band error naming that ticket.
COMP-3: a body's ` ```component <tag> ` blocks register components
(`watch` says so after the rest of the birth); a block whose tag is
not a component name, a name defined twice, and a name another
ticket defines are in-band errors — the last naming that ticket —
with nothing stored or allocated.
Yields exactly one event: `Created` or `Error`.

mdParams.pdDescription: The filter, in FILTER-3's language.

tickets.filters.delete.mdDescription: Delete a saved filter by name; an in-band error when there is none. Yields filter_deleted. A filter that names it stops resolving.

mdParams.pdDescription: The filter's name.

tickets.filters.get.mdDescription: One saved filter, by name (matched by its slug: `Open Builds` is `open-builds`), with its count; an in-band error when there is none.

mdParams.pdDescription: The filter's name, e.g. 'Shipped today'.

tickets.filters.list.mdDescription: Every saved filter of the caller's organization, by name: its filter, how many tickets in reach it admits, who saved it and when (`Needs you` among them until one is saved under that name).

tickets.filters.rename.mdDescription: Give a saved filter another name, keeping its filter and who saved it; refused in band when the new name is another filter's. Yields filter_saved with `renamed_from`. A filter that names the old name stops resolving.

mdParams.pdDescription: The filter's name now.
The name it takes.

tickets.filters.save.mdDescription: Save a filter under a name in the caller's organization — new, or replacing the one of that name (who first saved it is kept). Refused in band, nothing written: a filter the language cannot read (the chunk and where it stands are named), one holding `text`, a `saved "…"` that names none or makes a cycle. Yields filter_saved with the row.

mdParams.pdDescription: The filter, in FILTER-3's language, e.g. 'deployed app-prod today'.
The filter's name, e.g. 'Shipped today'; saving under a name that exists replaces it.

tickets.filters.schema.mdDescription: Get plugin or method schema. Pass {"method": "name"} for a specific method.

tickets.find.mdDescription:
Find tickets whose id or title contains the query (case-insensitive), optionally under a filter; summary rows, paged with after + limit.

SCALE-6: the jump palette's question, answered where the rows are
— so a client that does not hold every row (SCALE-7) can still
find one. Yields one `summary` row per ticket whose id or title
contains `query`, case-insensitively with ASCII folding (AGS-18's
rule, the palette's own), in (epic, seq) order — at most `limit`,
default 50, what the palette shows — then exactly one `page`
event: `remaining` plus the rows is the palette's total. `query`
is trimmed; empty or blank matches every ticket, so the palette
opens on the head of the store. `after` pages it exactly as
`list` (MNG-9) — a position, not a match — and one naming no
ticket is one in-band `error`. Ids and titles only: a jump aid,
not search over bodies.

FILTER-15: `filter` (the language's text, FILTER-10) keeps the text
matches the filter admits, in the same order, paged and counted as
without it — the needle tested only on the candidates the filter's
cells admit, never on the rest of the store. A filter not taken, or
one that asks `under` or `text`, is one in-band `error`; one that
narrows nothing (empty, a display part alone) is no filter.

mdParams.pdDescription: Cursor: start strictly after this ticket id, e.g. MNG-9 (optional).
A filter, e.g. 'not category done' (FILTER-3's language; optional): only the matches it admits.
At most this many tickets (default 50); the page event carries the next cursor (optional).
Substring of the ticket id or title, case-insensitive (ASCII), trimmed; empty matches every ticket.
The time zone a history filter's days are read in: an IANA name, UTC, or an offset (optional; default UTC).

tickets.get.mdDescription:
Get one ticket by id, or by path address SHORTCODE/path (e.g. PLEXUS/_MENGER/board).

Yields exactly one event: `Ticket` if found, `NotFound` otherwise.
WAVE-10: `id` may be a path address, `<SHORTCODE>/<path>` — the
shortcode case-insensitive, the path exact — naming the one ticket of
that shortcode that holds the path; `NotFound` carries the address.

mdParams.pdDescription: Ticket id, e.g. MNG-2 — or a path address, e.g. PLEXUS/_MENGER/board.

tickets.health.mdDescription:
Heartbeat — version, unix time, ticket count.

Returns the binary version, the server's unix time, and
how many tickets the store holds.

tickets.history.mdDescription:
A ticket's history: each status and kind transition (from, to, when, who, source, message, cause), oldest first, then those it caused in other tickets, then its queue records (MENGER-39), then history_end (when the log began; what a restore would put back; since when it has held its status).

MENGER-13: a ticket's history — every change of its status and its
kind since the log began, as the store keeps them. Yields one
`Transition` per transition of the ticket's, oldest first — `from` →
`to`, when, who (`actor`: a principal, `system`, or `anonymous` on one
kept before ACCESS-24, when login could be off; `name`), from where (`source`: app, api, pipeline,
cascade), why (`message`) and what caused it (`cause`, a transition
id) — then one per transition those caused in other tickets (a
cancel's cascade, a restore's), in the order written, then exactly one
`HistoryEnd { began_unix, restorable }`: when the log began (nothing
before it has a history), and for a canceled ticket the descendants
`set_status { restore_children: true }` would put back. `NotFound` for
an id that names no ticket (or one out of the caller's reach). From
the cache; `watch` carries each new `Transition`.

mdParams.pdDescription: Ticket id, e.g. MENGER-7.

tickets.inputs.mdDescription: A ticket's inputs — `tickets.inputs.<method>`: list, answer, clear, close, reopen (INPUT-3, ACCESS-14).

tickets.inputs.answer.mdDescription:
Answer an input: record a value (checked against its kind and options) with a rationale, the time, and where it came from (said by the server); yields input_changed.

INPUT-3: answers an input — records `value` against `ticket`'s input
`input`, with its `rationale` and the time. ACCESS-14: its `source`
is the server's — `app` for a person signed in through a provider,
`api` for an agent's key and for a call that proves no one. The value
is typed by the input's kind and checked against the options its
body declares: `{"type": "choice", "option": …}` names one,
`{"type": "multi", "options": […]}` a set (kept in the body's order,
each once; empty: none ticked), `{"type": "text", "text": …}` a
reply, not blank. Every answer is a history entry — a changed one,
and the same one again. Yields exactly one event: `InputChanged` (the
input as it is now, its answer and history included), `NotFound` for
a ticket that is none, or an in-band `Error` — the ticket declares no
such input, the value does not answer it, it is closed, or it was
removed from its body — and nothing is written. Never touches the
body. `tickets.watch` carries the `InputChanged`.

mdParams.pdDescription: The input's id in that ticket's body, e.g. landing.
Why (optional).
Ticket id, e.g. INPUT-9.

Typed by the input's kind: {"type": "choice", "option": "archive"} | {"type": "multi", "options": ["a", "b"]} | {"type": "text", "text": "a reply"}; through synapse, --value.type choice --value.option archive.

tickets.inputs.ask.mdDescription:
File a question for the owner on a ticket: a new text input appended to its body (one write, one revision); yields input_changed with the input.

APP-90: the chat composer's `/ask`. Appends `<m-input id="ask-N"
kind="text"><m-question>…</m-question></m-input>` to `ticket`'s
body — `N` the lowest no input of the ticket has had, so the id is
unique in it; the question escaped, so it is text and never markup —
through `amend`'s write (its revision, `asking` moved in it,
`amended` and `input_changed` broadcast). Yields exactly one event:
`InputChanged` (the new input, `open`), `NotFound`, or an in-band
`Error` — the body would pass `--max-body-bytes`, or its markup
elsewhere is malformed — and nothing is written.

mdParams.pdDescription: The question, one line (its whitespace collapsed), e.g. "Hold at cone 6 or 5?".
Ticket id, e.g. KILN-40.

tickets.inputs.clear.mdDescription:
Clear an input's answer (open again; kept in its history, with where it came from, said by the server); yields input_changed.

INPUT-3: clears an input's answer — `open` again, the clear in its
history, with its source (ACCESS-14: the server's, as for `answer`).
Yields exactly one event: `InputChanged`; `Input` when it held no
answer (nothing written); `NotFound`; or an in-band `Error` — no
such input, closed, removed.

mdParams.pdDescription: The input's id in that ticket's body.
Ticket id, e.g. INPUT-9.

tickets.inputs.close.mdDescription:
Close an input: freeze its answer (or its lack of one); yields input_changed.

INPUT-3: closes an input — frozen (a decision's DECIDED), with its
answer or without one; an answer or a clear is refused until it is
reopened. Yields exactly one event: `InputChanged`; `Input` when it
was closed already; `NotFound`; or an in-band `Error` — no such
input, removed.

mdParams.pdDescription: The input's id in that ticket's body.
Ticket id, e.g. INPUT-9.

tickets.inputs.list.mdDescription:
Every input (a body's <m-decision id> / <m-input id kind>) with its kind, question, options, recommendation, state, answer and history; filtered by ticket, shortcode, state and a filter on its ticket.

INPUT-3: the inputs store. Yields one `Input` per input of `ticket`
(every ticket's, without one) whose ticket is in the shortcode `epic`
and which is in `state` — its ticket, id, kind (`choice`, `multi`,
`text`), question, options (`{ value, label, recommended }`, the
body's order), recommendation, state (`open`, `answered`, `closed`,
`removed`), current answer (`{ value, rationale, source, at_unix }`,
`null` with none) and whole history, oldest first — in the store's
order of tickets, each ticket's inputs in its body's order and the
removed after. Nothing trails them; the stream's own `done` is the
whole answer. `NotFound` when `ticket` names no ticket. From the
cache; `tickets.watch` keeps a client's copy current with
`InputChanged`.

FILTER-15: `filter` (the language's text, FILTER-10) keeps the inputs
whose ticket the filter admits — each such ticket one lookup in the
filter's admitted cells; every other parameter as without it. A
filter not taken, or one that asks `under` or `text`, is one in-band
`error`; one that narrows nothing (empty, a display part alone) is no
filter.

mdParams.pdDescription: Only inputs of tickets in this shortcode (optional).
A filter on the input's ticket, e.g. 'kind build' (FILTER-3's language; optional): only inputs of tickets it admits.
Only inputs in this state: open | answered | closed | removed | withdrawn (optional; withdrawn: its ticket is canceled).
Only this ticket's inputs, e.g. INPUT-9 (optional).
The time zone a history filter's days are read in: an IANA name, UTC, or an offset (optional; default UTC).

tickets.inputs.reopen.mdDescription:
Reopen a closed input; yields input_changed.

INPUT-3: reopens a closed input — `answered` again when it holds an
answer, else `open`. Yields exactly one event: `InputChanged`;
`Input` when it was not closed; `NotFound`; or an in-band `Error` —
no such input, removed.

mdParams.pdDescription: The input's id in that ticket's body.
Ticket id, e.g. INPUT-9.

tickets.inputs.schema.mdDescription: Get plugin or method schema. Pass {"method": "name"} for a specific method.

tickets.label.mdDescription:
Add or remove a ticket's labels (e.g. needs-you), or many tickets' (ids; one write, all or none); yields labels_changed { ticket, added, removed } per ticket.

MENGER-12: moves a ticket's labels — free-form tags such as
`needs-you`, which puts the ticket on Home's "Needs you" panel.
`add` and `remove` are label names (letters, digits and `-`, at most
32 characters, folded to lower case); a label in both is added. The
ticket keeps its labels sorted, each once, at most 16. Yields exactly
one event: `LabelsChanged { ticket, added, removed }` — both empty
when nothing moved (every added label already held, every removed one
not), which writes and broadcasts nothing — `NotFound` if `id` names
no ticket, or an in-band `Error` naming every entry that is not a
label, or a result past 16; an error writes nothing. Moves
`updated_unix` and the ticket's filter cell (`label <name>`), nothing
else. `watch` carries every `LabelsChanged` that moved something.
ACT-2: `ids` instead of `id` moves each one's, in one write, all or
none, one `LabelsChanged` per ticket (`cells_stream`).

mdParams.pdDescription: Labels to add — letters, digits and -, at most 32 characters, lower-cased (e.g. ["needs-you"]) (optional).
Ticket id, e.g. MENGER-12 (or ids).
Ticket ids, instead of id: every one's labels move, in one write, all or none.
Labels to remove (optional).

tickets.list.mdDescription:
List tickets, optionally filtered by epic, status, parent and/or a filter; paged with after + limit, or at a position with at.

Yields one row event per match, ordered by (epic, seq), then
exactly one `page` event saying where the walk stands. The
`parent` filter (AGS-19) yields exactly that ticket's children —
since SCALE-4 the one way to read them (a row carries only their
`child_count`), and a page of them costs the page.

MNG-9 adds the page: `after` is the exclusive cursor (a ticket id
— the order is total and unique, so an id is a position), `limit`
caps the page, and `summary` swaps the `ticket` rows for `summary`
rows that carry every field but the body. ACCESS-29: a page is 1,000
rows unless `limit` says, and never past 10,000 ([`crate::limits`]).
An `after` naming no ticket
is one in-band `error` and nothing else. SCALE-14: the rows come
from the cache and the bodies from the database, read a page at a
time as the rows go out — the same events, never every body at
once.

FILTER-4: `filter` (the language's text, FILTER-10) narrows the
matches further — ANDed with `epic`, `status` and `parent`, which are
sugar beside it — answered from the cells, never by testing a
ticket; and `at` starts the page at a position among the matches
(0-based) instead of after a cursor. Given either, the page event
carries `first`, the page's first row's position among the matches;
`at` past the end is an empty page with `first = at` and `next:
null`; `at` with `after` is an in-band `error`, and so is a filter
the language does not take (every bad chunk named) or one that
asks `under` or `text` (each named, with where it lives). Given
neither, every event is what it was.

FILTER-24: with a filter, `keep` (a ticket id: the nav's open ticket)
is listed and counted as a match whatever the filter says of it — at
its place, in `first` and `remaining` — when it is inside `epic`,
`status` and `parent` and inside the caller's reach; otherwise, and
without a filter, it changes nothing.

mdParams.pdDescription: Cursor: start strictly after this ticket id, e.g. MNG-9 (optional).
Start at this position among the matches, 0-based, instead of after a cursor (optional; not with after); the page event carries first.
Epic prefix filter (optional).
A filter, e.g. 'ready and kind build and in SCALE' (FILTER-3's language; optional): ANDed with epic, status and parent; the page event then carries first.
With a filter: this ticket id is listed and counted as a match whatever the filter says of it, e.g. the open ticket (optional; one inside epic, status and parent).
At most this many tickets (default 1000, at most 10000); the page event carries the next cursor (optional).
Only this ticket's children, e.g. PERF-3 (optional).
Status filter: Pending | Ready | Coding | In Review | Blocked | Complete | Draft | Epic | Superseded | Canceled | Doc (optional).
Yield summary rows (every field but the body) instead of full tickets (optional).
The time zone a history filter's days are read in (today, yesterday, this week, a date): an IANA name, e.g. Europe/Berlin, UTC, or an offset, e.g. +02:00 (optional; default UTC).

tickets.nav.mdDescription: What the nav and the menus ask — `tickets.nav.<method>`: groups, extents, tree, counts, facets, member (ACCESS-16).

tickets.nav.counts.mdDescription:
Each shortcode's number of tickets matching a filter, in shortcode order — the filtered extents (every ticket without one).

FILTER-4: the filtered `extents`. Yields one `Count { epic, held }`
per shortcode that holds a match of `filter`, in shortcode order,
and nothing after them — the stream's own `done` ends it, as for
`extents`. Without a filter, each shortcode's tickets. A sum over
the kept counts of the cells the filter admits: no ticket is tested,
and the cost is the shortcodes and the cells, never the tickets.
With the counts, a client turns a position among the matches into a
(shortcode, rank) by prefix sums, and asks `list { filter, at }`. A
filter not taken, or one that asks `under` or `text`, is one in-band
`error` and nothing else. FILTER-24: `keep` (a ticket id inside the
caller's reach) is counted as a match whatever the filter says of it —
once — as `list { filter, keep }` pages it.

mdParams.pdDescription: A filter, e.g. 'ready and kind build' (FILTER-3's language; optional: every ticket).
This ticket id is counted as a match whatever the filter says of it, e.g. the open ticket (optional).
The time zone a history filter's days are read in: an IANA name, UTC, or an offset (optional; default UTC).

tickets.nav.extents.mdDescription:
Each shortcode's last sequence (a deleted ticket's too: numbers are never reused) and the holes below it, in shortcode order — where each shortcode ends in the store's order.

SCALE-16: where each shortcode ends in the store's order. Yields
one `Extent` per shortcode that holds a ticket, in shortcode order
— its highest sequence, read from the per-shortcode sequence
`create` allocates from (SCALE-3), so the cost is the number of
shortcodes. ACT-5: past every deleted number, which a shortcode's
`holes` name — sequences are dense but for them, so with these a
client turns a position in the store's order into a cursor without
walking to it:
prefix sums find the shortcode E and the row k, and `list { after:
"E-k" }` starts at row k + 1. Nothing trails the extents — there is
no cursor to hand back — so the stream's own `done` is the whole
answer, as for `groups` and `blockers`. No watch event keeps them:
`created` already carries the newborn's `epic` and `seq`.

tickets.nav.facets.mdDescription:
Menu counts: per field (status, category, kind, severity, blocked, ready, has commits, menger doc, in), the matches of base and filter without filter's own groups for that field, by value.

FILTER-4: the counts behind every menu (Linear's facets). For each
field — `status`, `category`, `kind`, `severity`, `blocked`, `ready`,
`has commits`, `menger doc` (FILTER-21), `in`, in that order — the
tickets matching `base` and `filter` with `filter`'s own groups for
that field set aside (a group is a field's own when every predicate
in it names that field; `base`'s are never set aside), counted by
value: one `Facet { field, value, held }` per value with `held` above
0 — `field` as the language spells it, `value` canonical (`Coding`,
`build`, `none`, `yes`/`no` for the four flags, the shortcode for
`in`), statuses in the store's order of statuses, shortcodes in
shortcode order — then the stream's done. A sum over kept cell
counts, never a ticket. A filter not taken, or one that asks `under`
or `text`, is one in-band `error` and nothing else.

mdParams.pdDescription: A filter that always applies, e.g. the global one (optional): never set aside.
The filter whose menus are counted (optional): its own groups for a field are set aside for that field's counts.
The time zone a history filter's days are read in: an IANA name, UTC, or an offset (optional; default UTC).

tickets.nav.groups.mdDescription:
One roll-up per shortcode: done/total over its subtree's work, its docs, its root (with the root's title, status and kind), and the host it nests under.

MNG-10: the nav's tree without its rows. Yields one `Group` per
shortcode row the nav draws, in shortcode order — `done/total` over
the row's whole subtree (SDLC-11: its work; `docs` counts its docs,
which have no completion), its scope (or doc) `root`, and the `host` ticket it
nests under when it is a sub-shortcode — exactly as AGS-20's
`plan()` computes them from every row. AGS-23: and the root's own
row — its title, status and kind (`root_row`) — which the nav draws
as the shortcode's top row, so its top level needs nothing else.
Nothing trails the groups:
unlike `list` there is no cursor to hand back, so the stream's own
`done` is the whole answer, as for `blockers`. `watch` keeps a
client's copy current with `GroupChanged`. ACCESS-10: the shortcodes
the caller sees; a root or host out of reach is none (the shortcode
at the top for this caller).

tickets.nav.member.mdDescription:
Which of these tickets a filter admits: one member { id, matched } per id, in the order given (an unknown id: false); at most 1000 ids.

FILTER-15: which of some tickets a filter admits — what a page that
shows tickets it did not list (a ticket page, its blockers, its
unlocks) asks of the global filter. Yields one `Member { id, matched
}` per id, in the order given — `id` as given, `matched` whether the
filter admits the ticket it names; an id (or `SHORTCODE/path`
address) that names no ticket is `matched: false` — and nothing
after them: the stream's own `done` ends it. Each id is one lookup in
the filter's admitted cells, never a test of the ticket. At most
1,000 ids: more, a filter not taken, or one that asks `under` or
`text`, is one in-band `error` and nothing else.

mdParams.pdDescription: A filter, e.g. 'status Ready' (FILTER-3's language; empty: every ticket).
Ticket ids (or SHORTCODE/path addresses), e.g. ["FILTER-4", "FILTER-5"]; at most 1000.
The time zone a history filter's days are read in: an IANA name, UTC, or an offset (optional; default UTC).

tickets.nav.schema.mdDescription: Get plugin or method schema. Pass {"method": "name"} for a specific method.

tickets.nav.tree.mdDescription:
The nav under a filter: a parent's children (or a shortcode's top level) that match or hold a match, each with matched and below (matches strictly under it), then a page; matches_only: the matches nearest below instead, then the hosted shortcodes drawn there.

FILTER-13: the nav under a filter — the rows the nav would show at an
address unfiltered (`parent`: that ticket's children, as `list {
parent }` gives them; `epic`: the shortcode's top level — its root,
or, for a shortcode with none, its tickets as `list { epic }` gives
them), only those that match `filter` or hold a match below them, in
the store's order. One `Node { summary, matched, below }` per row —
`matched` whether the row matches, `below` how many matches are
strictly under it — then one `Page { next, remaining }`, paged as
`list` pages (`after` a ticket id, at most `limit`). Answered from the
kept tree: a parent's children under a filter are (C(P) ∩ M) ∪ the
holders of every admitted cell, and `below` a sum over the row's
tally — no subtree is walked. Exactly one of `parent` and `epic`; a
filter not taken, or one that asks `text`, is one in-band `error` and
nothing else.

FILTER-23: `matches_only` — the nav that draws only matches, no
ticket that only holds them. At `parent`, the matches nearest below
it: its children that match and, in place of a child that does not,
that child's own nearest matches, at any depth, in the store's order
— then the hosted shortcodes whose row is drawn there (hosted at the
parent, or at a ticket between that is not drawn), in shortcode
order, each as its root's node, whether or not it holds a match. At
`epic`, the root when it matches, else the top of the shortcode: what
the root's `parent` address answers (a shortcode with no root: its
tickets that match). Paged the same way. Off, `tree` is FILTER-13's,
byte for byte.

FILTER-24: `keep`, with `matches_only` — a ticket id (the nav's open
ticket) answered as if it matched: a row where a match would be, its
own nearest matches answered under it rather than above, a hosted
shortcode placed at it; its node still says `matched: false`. A
match, a shortcode's root, an id naming no ticket, or one outside the
caller's reach changes nothing.

mdParams.pdDescription: Cursor: start strictly after this ticket id (optional).
A shortcode's top level: its root, or its tickets when it has none (or give parent).
A filter, e.g. 'status Ready and under SCALE' (FILTER-3's language; empty: every ticket).
With matches_only: this ticket id is drawn as if it matched — where a match would be, its nearest matches under it — e.g. the open ticket (optional; its node still says matched false).
At most this many rows; the page event carries the next cursor (optional).

Only matches (optional, default false): a ticket that does not match is not a row, and the matches below it are answered in its place, at the nearest ancestor that matches or at the top of the shortcode; then the hosted shortcodes drawn there.
Whose children, e.g. FILTER-9 (or give epic).
The time zone a history filter's days are read in: an IANA name, UTC, or an offset (optional; default UTC).

tickets.queue.mdDescription:
Queue a ticket for the owner — urgency whenever | today | now | blocking (blocking names the input that answers it), and why, with the inputs it asks (repeat --input; --blocking the one you are idle on) and views of mockups to look at (repeat --mockup); queued again it is raised, never lowered, and its inputs and views added; yields queued { entry, ticket, action }.

MENGER-39: puts a ticket in front of the owner — at an urgency, for a
reason; `blocking` names the input that answers it. Queued again: the
urgency raised, never lowered. APP-86: several inputs, in order, and
the one the caller is idle on. Yields one `queued`, or an `error`.

mdParams.pdDescription: The one input the caller is idle on — among them; required with urgency blocking when there are several (optional).
Ticket id, e.g. MENGER-39.
The inputs on the ticket whose answers are asked, in order — repeat the flag (required for blocking); closing every one unqueues the ticket.
The inputs are this message's, in a chat on the ticket (CHAT-20), e.g. 812 (optional).
Views of mockups the owner answers looking at — repeat the flag: T#mN, T (a whole-page body), or mockup:T#N@W (optional).
Why the owner should look (required).
app | api | pipeline (optional, default api).
whenever | today | now | blocking.

tickets.queued.mdDescription:
The owner's queue, most urgent first, then oldest: a queue_row { entry, ticket } each, then queue_end { count, snoozed, now_unix }.

MENGER-39: the owner's queue, most urgent first, then the oldest.

mdParams.pdDescription: Include the snoozed ones (optional; default true — each marked by its snoozed_until_unix).

tickets.request_changes.mdDescription:
Request changes on a queued ticket: the body kept as a comment on its conversation (intent changes) and the ticket unqueued (action changes_requested), in one write; its input stays open; yields changes_requested { id, comment, entry, by, at_unix }.

APP-23: hands a queued ticket back — a comment (intent `changes`) on its conversation and the entry unqueued, one write.

mdParams.pdDescription: What to change (markdown).
The queued ticket, e.g. APP-21.
app | api | pipeline (optional, default api).

tickets.reshortcode.mdDescription:
Move tickets into another shortcode, renumbered there in the order given (a scope moved into a new code becomes its root; --new-scope makes the shortcode first; a root moves with --with-children as a rename); old ids keep resolving (get says moved_from); all or none; yields reshortcoded { moves, tickets }.

ACT-6: tickets moved into another shortcode ([`crate::store::Reshortcoded`]'s module).

mdParams.pdDescription: Answer the moves it would make (old id → new key, in order; no tickets) and write nothing (optional; default false).
Ticket ids, in the order they take their new numbers, e.g. ["THEME-9", "THEME-10"].
Why (optional).
Make the shortcode first: its root a new scope of this title under parent (optional).
Where the moved tickets hang, inside the target (optional; default its root) — with new_scope, where the new scope hangs.
The shortcode they move into, e.g. LOOK (any short form of its address).
Each one's descendants in its own shortcode move with it (optional; default false: they stay, under the nearest ancestor that stays).

Restore archived tickets — each named (or a filter's archived ones) back in every view with its archived ancestors; with_children, the subtree archived with it; yields restored { ids, ancestors, still_archived, by, dry_run }.

ARCHIVE-2: the ancestor chain comes back, never its other children (ARCHIVE-1); what stays archived below is named (still_archived). dry_run: the answer, nothing written.

mdParams.pdDescription: Answer what the write would do and write nothing (optional; default false).
Instead of ids: the archived tickets this filter admits, e.g. 'archived within 7d by me'.
Archived ticket ids, e.g. ["KILN-4"] (or filter).
With a filter: the most tickets it may name (default 500).
Why — kept in each transition (optional).
The time zone a history filter's days are read in (optional; default UTC).
Bring back the descendants archived in the same write as each (optional; default false: they stay, named).

tickets.revisions.mdDescription: A ticket's revisions — `tickets revisions list | get | diff | restore` (TICKETS-7, activation/revisions.rs).

tickets.revisions.diff.mdDescription:
What changed between two revisions: field by field, the frontmatter key by key, the body as a line diff with words within a changed line; yields revision_diff { diff }.

TICKETS-7: `from` → `to` — `to` omitted, the latest; `from` omitted,
the revision before `to`. Each field that differs with its value in
each; the body's frontmatter key by key; the body's line diff in hunks
(three lines of context; a line changed in place carries its words),
of its source — or, `text: true`, of the text a reader sees (no
markup, no scripts or styles, no frontmatter). At most 4,000 lines of
hunks (`truncated` says so).

mdParams.pdDescription: The older revision (optional; default the one before to).
Ticket id, e.g. DEPLOY-9.
Diff the visible text instead of the source (optional; default false).
The newer revision (optional; default the latest).

tickets.revisions.get.mdDescription:
The ticket exactly as it was at a revision; yields revision_at { revision, ticket }.

TICKETS-7: every field a revision keeps (title, body, status, kind,
severity, parent, blockers, labels, commits) as it was then; the rest
(its id, address, children, placement) as it is now. A body that uses
a component or a theme renders with today's definitions. `NotFound`
for a ticket out of reach; an `Error` for a revision it does not have.

mdParams.pdDescription: Ticket id, e.g. DEPLOY-9.
The revision's number, from 1.

tickets.revisions.list.mdDescription:
A ticket's revisions, newest first: rev, when, who, from where, why, what changed, the body's hash, size and +/- lines; then revisions_end { count, latest, next }.

TICKETS-7: yields one `Revision` per revision of the ticket, newest
first — at most `limit` (100; at most 500), below `before` when
given — then `RevisionsEnd { count, latest, next }` (`next`: the
`before` of the next page, `null` at the oldest). A ticket older than
revisions has none until it is first changed; that write keeps its
version before (`source: baseline`) and its own. Transitions stay in
`history`. `NotFound` for a ticket out of the caller's reach. From
storage, not the cache.

mdParams.pdDescription: Only revisions older than this number (optional; the page before, from revisions_end's next).
Ticket id, e.g. DEPLOY-9 (a deleted ticket's too).
At most this many (optional; default 100, at most 500).

tickets.revisions.restore.mdDescription:
Put a revision's fields back — all it keeps but its commits, or those named — as one update, itself a new revision; yields revision_restored { ticket, from_rev, changed, rev }.

TICKETS-7: writes the chosen fields of revision `rev` (default: title,
body, status, kind, severity, parent, blocked_by, labels — each that
differs from now) through `update`'s rules: a parent that no longer
exists, a blocker cycle, a duplicate input id, a component another
ticket defines are refused, naming why, and nothing is written. The
revision it keeps says what it restored, from which revision, and
`message`. Nothing differing writes nothing (`changed: []`, `rev:
null`). A deleted ticket is undeleted first; commits are never
restored; a parent is moved, never cleared.

mdParams.pdDescription: Which fields (optional; default every one it keeps but commits): title, body, status, kind, severity, parent, blocked_by, labels.
Ticket id, e.g. DEPLOY-9.
Why, kept in the revision after what it restored (optional).
The revision to restore from.
Where the change comes from: app | api | pipeline (optional, default api).

tickets.search.mdDescription:
Search inside tickets: the tickets whose title or body holds every word of the query (prefixes and typos too), best first, each with the passage that matched; optionally under a filter, paged with offset + limit.

SEARCH-2: search inside tickets — the tickets whose title or body's
text holds every word of `query`, best first, from the search index
in the database (the store's `search`): a word matches itself and as
a prefix; one of four letters or more that the index does not know,
or holds in only a few tickets, also matches the index's words one
edit away (two from eight letters); a word joined by `-` `_` `.` `/`, or a `"quoted phrase"`,
is a phrase. Tickets matched without a correction come first, then
the rest; BM25 within each, a title weighing 4 to the text's 1.

Yields one `hit { summary, title, snippet, corrected }` per ticket of
the page, then one `searched { matched, next, words }`. `filter` (the
language's text, FILTER-10) keeps the matches it admits (`under`
too); one not taken, or one that asks `text`, is one in-band `error`
and nothing else. `limit` is [`SEARCH_LIMIT`] unless given, at most
[`SEARCH_MAX`]; `offset` skips that many matches.

mdParams.pdDescription: A filter, e.g. 'not category done' (FILTER-3's language; optional): only the matches it admits.
At most this many hits (default 20, at most 100) (optional).
Skip this many matches — the searched event's next (optional).
Words to find, e.g. 'plcement wave' — each also as a prefix; a misspelt one also as the words a typo away; FILTER-23 or "a phrase" as a phrase.
The time zone a history filter's days are read in: an IANA name, UTC, or an offset (optional; default UTC).

tickets.set_kind.mdDescription:
Set a ticket's kind; everything kept by kind moves with it (to a doc: status Doc; from a doc: the status given, else Epic for a scope and Pending otherwise).

SDLC-13: changes a ticket's kind — the one write that does — and
everything kept by kind with it, in the one write. Yields exactly one
event: `KindChanged { ticket, previous }`, `NotFound` if `id` names no
ticket, or an in-band `Error` naming what it refuses. The status goes
with the kind across the doc line: to a doc it becomes `Doc` (a
`status` other than `Doc` is an `Error`); from a doc it becomes
`status` when given (never `Doc`), else `Epic` for a scope and
`Pending` for any other kind; between two other kinds it stays unless
`status` is given (`Doc` an `Error`). Refused: a ticket that waits on
a blocker, or that a ticket waits on, becoming a doc (both named); a
shortcode's root becoming a kind that roots nothing (the shortcode
named — doc ↔ scope on a root is allowed); a ticket holding a path
address becoming work; an unknown kind or status. A lower-seq ticket
that becomes a scope or a doc becomes its shortcode's root. The kind
(and status) it already has writes and sends nothing: `KindChanged`
with `previous` equal to its kind. `watch` carries `KindChanged`
first, then the `GroupChanged`, `PlacementsChanged` and (filtered)
`Entered` / `Left` it caused, as for a status change.

mdParams.pdDescription: Ticket id, e.g. IDENTITY-1.
New kind: scope | execution | build | gap | spike | doc (case-insensitive).
Why, kept in the transitions (optional).
Where the change comes from: app | api | pipeline (optional, default api) — kept in the transitions.

Its status with the new kind (optional): Pending | Ready | Coding | In Review | Blocked | Complete | Draft | Epic | Superseded | Canceled — or Doc, the only one a doc takes; omitted, a doc becomes Doc, a doc becoming work becomes Epic (a scope) or Pending, and work keeps its own.

tickets.set_parent.mdDescription:
Set a ticket's parent — the ticket it is an output of; adopts a parentless ticket or moves one.

MNG-12: files an existing ticket as an output of `parent` — the
verb AGS-19 left out. Adopts a ticket born parentless, or moves
one. Yields exactly one event: `ParentChanged` (the child, with the
parent it had before), `NotFound` if `id` names no ticket, or an
in-band `Error` when the parent does not exist or the chain would
make the ticket its own ancestor. `watch` also carries the parents'
side: `ChildrenChanged` for the new parent and `ChildRemoved` for
the old one — each the parent's id and new `child_count` (SCALE-4).

mdParams.pdDescription: Ticket id to file, e.g. AGS-2.
Id of the ticket to file it under; any epic, must exist.

tickets.set_status.mdDescription:
Set a ticket's status (not a doc's: a doc has no lifecycle); Canceled cancels its open descendants in the same write, and leaving Canceled may restore them (restore_children).

Yields exactly one event: `StatusChanged`, `NotFound`, or `Error`.
SDLC-7: the vocabulary is nine — the worker states `Coding` and
`In Review` included — and the write is free: any status to any
other, nothing gated (SDLC-4 owns transitions). SDLC-11: a doc has no
lifecycle — `set_status` on one is an in-band `Error`, whatever the
status — and `Doc` is a doc's own: setting it on any other kind is an
in-band `Error` too. Neither writes anything.

MENGER-13: the change is a transition — the caller's (always
someone, ACCESS-24), from `source` (`api` unless the call says `app` or
`pipeline`), with its `message` — kept in the log and said on `watch`
right after the `StatusChanged`. Into `Canceled`, the ticket's open
inputs are withdrawn and every descendant still open work is
canceled in the same write, each a transition of `system`'s naming
the cause. Out of `Canceled`, its withdrawn inputs come back; with
`restore_children`, so do the descendants its cancel canceled (and
nothing has moved since), to the statuses they had.

mdParams.pdDescription: Ticket id, e.g. MNG-2.
Why, kept in the transition (optional).
Leaving Canceled: also put back, to the statuses they had, the descendants its cancel canceled and nothing has moved since (optional, default false; history's history_end names them).
Where the change comes from: app | api | pipeline (optional, default api) — kept in the transition.

New status: Pending | Ready | Coding | In Review | Blocked | Complete | Draft | Epic | Superseded | Canceled (the canonical spelling; through -p, the app or REST any case, `active` is Coding; never Doc, a doc's own).

tickets.snooze.mdDescription:
Snooze a queued ticket for some minutes (1 to a week): off the alerting surfaces, still queued; yields snoozed { entry, ticket }.

MENGER-39: a queued ticket off the alerting surfaces for a while; it
stays queued. Yields one `snoozed`, or an `error`.

mdParams.pdDescription: Ticket id, e.g. MENGER-39.
How long, in minutes.
app | api | pipeline (optional, default api).
